name: Rosecliff

dates.note: The style node's exemplar gives 1902, the completion year; the Wikipedia infobox gives 'Built 1898-1902' and a Southern Methodist University photograph caption read the same day says 'built in 1899-1902'. The two start years disagree by one and neither is edited.

refs.title: Rosecliff - Wikipedia
refs.note: Gives the address as 548 Bellevue Avenue, the architect as 'Stanford White, McKim, Mead & White', and - worth carrying - the architectural style as 'French Baroque Revival', not Beaux-Arts.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 73000059; added February 6, 1973; contributing property of the Bellevue Avenue Historic District (ID72000023), as the Wikipedia infobox prints it
refs.note: Read from the infobox, not from the National Register's own database.

refs.title: Rosecliff - National Register of Historic Places Inventory, Rhode Island Historical Preservation & Heritage Commission
refs.note: The state commission's own copy of the Register nomination, indexed under 'Newport / Bellevue Avenue / Rosecliff'. Found by search; the PDF itself was not extracted, so nothing is quoted from it.

note: Written for WP-11.2 Tranche 2. Worth carrying: the National Register classifies Rosecliff as French Baroque Revival while this corpus files it under beaux-arts-american, and the style node's own note calls it 'after the Grand Trianon at Versailles'. Both readings are about the same building and the register's is the one a checker can cite.
